payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source mug visibly positioned to the right of the same headphones in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Fail when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug is not positioned to their right, including when a right-side mug cannot reliably be identified as the source mug. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish whether the source mug is positioned to the right. Do not infer source-mug identity or fulfillment from color or position alone, or from unrelated/newly generated mugs.
node.binding: Compare the source image's large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with the edited mugs, allowing for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting. Compare the same headphones and determine whether the source mug is visibly to their right. Do not treat color alone, an indistinct blur, or a different-looking mug as proof of source-mug identity. A pass means the requested placement is fulfilled.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows two small mugs: one to the left of the headphones and one to the right. The source mug is a large light-blue mug with a distinctive body and handle, but the edited mugs look different, and the blue-looking shape at far left is an indistinct blur. The image does not reliably establish which, if either, is the source mug, so its position relative to the headphones cannot be determined.

d1-progress: The node’s conservative identity rule is appropriate, but it appears overconstrained for this case: the edited image shows a strong blurred blue remnant at the mug’s former location and a mug-shaped object to the right of the headphones, while the original large blue mug is absent as a clearly intact object. Together these are evidence of a likely attempted move with incomplete/uncertain execution, not proof of no progress; the trace currently collapses that evidence to unknown. Refine the binding/criteria to assess the scene-level transformation jointly (former-location remnant, destination candidate, and source-object disappearance/continuity), allowing a partial-progress judgment when these cues coherently support an attempted relocation even if identity or final placement is not certain. Keep unknown for genuinely inconclusive or conflicting cues, and do not treat a destination mug or color/position alone as sufficient. The high-confidence unknown merits review of the evidence-to-status calibration, not simply lowering confidence or forcing the reference label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
